subject: How to perform merge operations on PositionDataFrame

messages.author: 510f43c000020d39
messages.subject: How to perform merge operations on PositionDataFrame
parts:
I would like to merge additional sample information (a data.frame object) into the pixelData (a Cardinal::PositionDataFrame object) of a Cardinal::MSImagingExperiment object.

If pixelData(mse) was a base data.frame object, then merge() or dplyr::left_join() could be used. However, neither merge() nor dplyr::left_join() work on Cardinal::PositionDataFrame objects.

Since Cardinal::PositionDataFrame inherits from S4Vectors::DataFrame, I thought the merge() method described in the S4Vectors manual (see page 12 under "DataFrame-utils") could work. However, I'm not sure the S4Vectors manual is accurate: ?S4Vectors::merge only shows a method for signature Vector,Vector but not for S4Vectors::DataFrame. Running S4Vectors::merge(pixelData(mse), sample_info, by.x = "run", by.y = "section") yields an error

Error in as(merge(as(x, "data.frame"), y, ...), class(x)) : no method or default for coercing “data.frame” to “PositionDataFrame”

Any help appreciated!

messages.author: db2a70d9b31cb1f7
messages.subject: Re: How to perform merge operations on PositionDataFrame
parts:
Hi Benjamin,

this works for me to add a new dataframe (df) which has to be already sorted for x and y as they appear in coord(mse):

pixelData(mse) <- PositionDataFrame(coord=coord(mse), run=run(mse), values=df)


For adding a single vector:

pixelData(test3cut)$newcolumn = name_vector

I hope this helps.
Melanie

messages.subject: Re: How to perform merge operations on PositionDataFrame
parts:
Hi, Melanie,

Thanks for your response.

Yes, I was aware that a single column could be added via the $ operator as you suggested.

I specifically asked about merge()-like operations (and specifically left_join()) because I have a separate dataframe of metadata about pixels in my dataset, and I want to merge columns from that dataframe into pixelData, but only for pixels that exist in pixelData - this operation is exactly what a left_join() means (see https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/reference/join.html#join-types). Currently, to merge in such metadata, the operation is rather cumbersome:

# given 2 existing variables
# - metadata: data.frame. columns = run, x, y, [other variables]
#     Assume that for a given combination of run, x, and y, there is only 1 row. I.e., metadata = dplyr::distinct(metadata, run, x, y)
# - mse: Cardinal::MSImagingExperiment

tmp <-
  mse %>%
    Cardinal::pixelData() %>%
    tibble::as_tibble() %>%
    dplyr::left_join(metadata, by = c("run", "x", "y"))

Cardinal::pixelData(mse) <- Cardinal::PositionDataFrame(
  run = dplyr::pull(tmp, run),
  coord = dplyr::select(tmp, x, y),
  dplyr::select(tmp, -c(run, x, y))
)

If anyone has a better way, please share!

messages.author: 6033d3c0e7d242fa
messages.subject: Re: How to perform merge operations on PositionDataFrame
parts:
Because of how run() and coord() are handled differently in a PostionDataFrame, you cannot do a straightforward join.

I'd say you have the right idea--converting to a ordinary data.frame (or tibble), and then converting back to a PositionDataFrame.

I'll note that there is some fragility in your approach in that it assumes the names of the run and coordinate columns, which are not actually guaranteed (and why they are typically accessed via accessor functions). While "run", "x", "y" are usually a safe assumption, this isn't 100% guaranteed to work. This shouldn't be a problem if used primarily on your own datasets/code.

I'll also note that DataFrame (from which PositionDataFrame extends) is more permissive in its columns than a tibble. The dplyr functions will fail on some data frames with S4 columns (which is part of why they were deprecated in Cardinal 2.6). Again, this isn't a problem if you're primarily using it on your own datasets/code.

-Kylie
